snowboardHowTest.title: GNU Riders Choice Review

snowboardingProfiles.testLimitations: One disclosed demo day; not a same-season 25/26 sample.
snowboardingProfiles.observations: Pretty fast and stable for a twin; good crud handling; jump landings solid and forgiving; medium-large jumps a sweet spot; decent but not deep-pow float; jibbing is not its strongest area.

snowboardingJunkie.observations: Responsive/smooth turns on piste but average low-speed maneuverability; jumps, switch, landings and buttering were positives; jib felt comparatively stiff; float was acceptable in ankle-depth snow but not the best choice for deeper Niseko powder.
snowboardingJunkie.seasonMatch: unconfirmed; do not label as a 2025/26 test

snowboardHow.disclosure: Author reports riding a rented sample for a few days and consulting other instructors; size, model year and conditions are not given.
snowboardHow.observations: Positive descriptions include stability at speed, edge control on hard/icy snow, park versatility and pop; limitations are deeper snow and very technical freeride. Construction details are excluded because the page's G2 Asym ECO claim conflicts with the official 25/26 3-D Delightwood Asym Chip terminology.
snowboardHow.seasonMatch: unconfirmed; directional-only, not a verified 25/26 test

scoringEvidence.siteScoreDecision: Keep current site scores (stability 8, response 8, float 7, park 7.5, forgiveness 6.5, value 8) as low-confidence editorial estimates. None of the three review sources is a verified 25/26 test: Snowboarding Profiles discloses a 2024 157.5 sample from 2023-03-23, SnowboardingJunkie discloses 154.5 but no model year, and SnowboardHow discloses a few days on a rental but no size/year/conditions. Qualitative findings are directionally consistent with an all-mountain freestyle board with jump/switch strengths and moderate powder/jib limits; do not map external totals or unlike scales linearly. Value remains especially uncertain without Chinese-market price provenance.
scoringEvidence.siteFlexNote: Official GNU scale for 157.5 is 6/10. Current site value is retained pending a catalog-wide brand-to-site flex normalization policy.

imageEvidence.reuseDecision: The historic official product page/video provide model artwork, but no explicit third-party image reuse license was found. Keep seed's AI placeholders until authorized assets or original photography are available.

seedMappingNotes: The representative seed size 157.5 is the median of the five standard-width sizes. Its official waist is 25.5 cm (255 mm), centered setback 0, sidecut pair 7.8/8.2 m and contact length 119 cm.

The official 25/26 eight-row table is now mirrored in prototype and YAML sizeSpecs with exact standard/W size identities and unit-qualified source columns; a direct official EU B-grade listing exposes the full season-specific table. Its B-grade price/condition is not applied to the normal seed.

GNU calls 119 cm contact length. Do not relabel it as effective edge. The existing seed effectiveEdge 1200 mm is an unverified legacy value and remains pending rather than being overwritten with contact length.

The official page does not provide board mass. Existing seed weight 2860 g is unverified; the Snowboarding Profiles test measured 3080 g on a 2024 157.5 sample, which is not evidence for the 25/26 board and must not be backdated.
Official size-specific GNU flex for 157.5 is 6/10; retain the site's 6.5 until a consistent mapping rule is approved.

Existing base, fiberglass, warranty and CNY price strings/values are not completely supported by the accessible 25/26 official spec table. Preserve them with explicit uncertainty; do not infer/convert regional prices or old-generation construction.
